gauge.name: Utoy Creek at Great Southwest Parkway near Atlanta

impacts.statement: Record flooding occurs with widespread inundation of the industrial park complex along the creek upstream and downstream from the gage on Great Southwest Parkway. Flood waters will top the Great Southwest Parkway bridge and the road will be under 4 feet of water. County officials will have the road closed. Numerous  commerical buildings near the creek will be flooded with up to 3 feet of water. This flooding will be similar to September 2009.

Major flooding begins with widespread inundation of the industrial park complex along the creek upstream and downstream from the gage on Great Southwest Parkway. Flood waters will top the Great Southwest Parkway bridge and the road will be under a foot of water. County officials will have it closed. Several commerical buildings near the creek will begin to flood.

Significant flooding expands further into the woodlands along the creek upstream and downstream from the gage on Great Southwest Parkway. The Great Southwest Parkway bridge begins to form an obstacle and act like a dam causing some backwater and erosion eddies to the sides of the bridge. County officials will likely have it closed. The water level will begin to flood the road and some industrial park buildings near the creek.

Moderate flooding begins. Significant flooding occurs in the woodlands along the creek upstream and downstream from the gage on Great Southwest Parkway. The water level will reach the bottom Great Southwest Parkway bridge and county official may close it. This would impact the industrial park complex in this area.
Minor flooding continues to expand further into the woodlands along the creek upstream and downstream from the gage on Great Southwest Parkway.
Flood stage is reached. Minor flooding begins in the woodlands along the creek upstream and downstream from the gage on Great Southwest Parkway.
Bankfull conditions are reached along the creek upstream and downstream from the gage on Great Southwest  Parkway.

value.label: North American Vertical Datum of 1988
value.description: A fixed reference for elevations determined by geodetic leveling. The datum was derived from a general adjustment of the first-order terrestrial leveling nets of the United States, Canada, and Mexico. In the adjustment, only the height of the primary tidal bench mark, referenced to the International Great Lakes Datum of 1985 (IGLD 85) local mean sea level height value, at Father Point, Rimouski, Quebec, Canada was held fixed, thus providing minimum constraint. NAVD 88 and IGLD 85 are identical. However, NAVD 88 bench mark values are given in Helmert orthometric height units while IGLD 85 values are in dynamic heights. See International Great Lakes Datum of 1985, National Geodetic Vertical Datum of 1929, and geopotential difference. NAVD 88 should not be used as Mean Sea Level.

value.label: Station Datum
value.description: A fixed base elevation at a tide station to which all water level measurements are referred. The datum is unique to each station and is established at a lower elevation than the water is ever expected to reach. It is referenced to the primary bench mark at the station and is held constant regardless of changes to the water level gauge or tide staff. The datum of tabulation is most often at the zero of the first tide staff installed.

gauge.forecastReliability: Forecasts are not available. Only observed stages are available for this point.
